properties.description: Widowed, Catherine McCarty leaves New York with her sons for Indianapolis.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 16.

properties.description: The family moves to Kansas, where it is recorded in the census at Wichita in 1870.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 17.

properties.nom: From Wichita to Santa Fe by way of Denver
properties.description: Catherine's tuberculosis drives the family toward the dry air of the West: Denver, then south to Santa Fe.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 17.

properties.nom: From Santa Fe to Silver City by the Rio Grande
properties.description: Shortly after the wedding, the family travels down the Rio Grande, then turns west toward the mining town of Silver City.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 17.

properties.description: Having escaped from the Silver City jail, Henry makes his way to Arizona and the area around Camp Grant.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 18.

properties.nom: Back to New Mexico and down the Pecos
properties.description: After Cahill's death, the Kid crosses back into New Mexico, joins Jesse Evans's “Boys” near La Mesilla and follows them to the lower Pecos.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 19-23.

properties.nom: From the Pecos to the Ruidoso
properties.description: From Seven Rivers, the Kid rides up the Hondo and the Ruidoso to the Coe ranch.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 27.

properties.description: On the morning of February 18, 1878, Tunstall leaves the Río Feliz heading north with his men and nine horses.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 37.

properties.nom: The Stinking Springs prisoners: Fort Sumner, Las Vegas, Santa Fe
properties.description: The prisoners are taken back to Fort Sumner, then by wagon to Las Vegas, and from there by train to Santa Fe.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 102-105.

properties.nom: By train from Santa Fe to La Mesilla
properties.description: On March 28, 1881, two deputy marshals take Billy and Billy Wilson by train down the Rio Grande valley.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 106.
properties.note: The railroad did not yet reach La Mesilla; the last stretch was by coach.

properties.nom: From La Mesilla to Lincoln, under escort
properties.description: Condemned, Billy is taken to Lincoln in a wagon, handcuffed and chained to the seat, guarded by seven men, including Billy Mathews and Bob Olinger, his sworn enemies.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 108-109.

properties.nom: The escaped prisoner returns to Fort Sumner
properties.description: After his escape, Billy rides down the north slope of the Capitan Mountains, crosses the Ruidoso above San Patricio and reaches the ranch of his friend John Meadows on the Peñasco (May 2, 1881). Instead of fleeing to Mexico, he then heads north to Fort Sumner and his shepherd friends.
properties.sources: Utley, Robert M. (2015), Wanted: The Outlaw Lives of Billy the Kid and Ned Kelly, New Haven, Yale University Press, PDF p. 112-113.
